sections.title: What privacy-first web analytics actually means
sections.content:
**Privacy-first web analytics** measures aggregate site usage — pages, referrers, campaigns, simple goals — without building an ad-tech identity graph. **Website analytics without cookies** is the implementation most buyers mean: no long-lived analytics cookie on the visitor’s device. **Privacy-friendly analytics** is the broader marketing phrase. It can mean cookieless by default (Fathom, Plausible, Umami, Ahrefs Web Analytics) or a lighter product that still uses first-party cookies unless you opt out (DataFast’s default script).

That is different from “GDPR-compliant GA4.” A privacy-first stack often reduces consent-banner friction because you collect less persistent identity in the first place. It does not replace a privacy policy, a DPA, or legal review. For the method itself — including accuracy trade-offs on returning visitors — read [cookieless analytics](/learn/cookieless-analytics/). If EU transfers or banners are why you are leaving Google Analytics, also read [GA4 alternatives for GDPR](/learn/ga4-alternatives-gdpr/).

Vendor copy that says “no cookie banner required” is **not legal advice**. Other scripts on the same page can still set cookies. [Fathom’s cookie FAQ](https://usefathom.com/docs/troubleshooting/cookies) (opened **24 November 2026**) says its embed does not use cookies or similar, and that other scripts may still need a banner.

sections.title: A clear pick for each use case
sections.content:
### Website analytics without cookies (hosted, no server)

**Pick [Fathom Analytics](https://usefathom.com/ref/U4V5UE)** when you want cookieless pageviews, UTMs, and events on vendor infrastructure, especially if you run **many sites**. [Fathom pricing](https://usefathom.com/pricing) (24 November 2026) starts at **$15/month** for **100,000** pageviews on **Standard**, with **every analytics feature** and **50 sites**. **Business** is **$39/month** at the same 100k stop and adds 10 team seats plus you, roles, site access control, a team audit log, higher API limits, and priority email. Custom events **count toward** the pageview allowance. Trial: **7 days**, card required.

**Pick [Plausible Cloud](/tools/plausible/)** when traffic is small enough that **$9/month at 10k pageviews** matters more than Fathom’s 100k floor, or when you want **EU-owned hosting** and an open-source path. At **100k** pageviews the widget is **Starter $19 / Growth $29 / Business $39** — so a **solo** site at 100k is **cheaper on Fathom Standard ($15)** than on Plausible Starter ($19). Plausible still wins the **10k** band and the **self-host / AGPL** fork. Head-to-head: [Plausible vs Fathom](/compare/plausible-vs-fathom/).

### Privacy-friendly analytics plus payments

**Pick [DataFast](https://datafa.st/?via=analyticsvs)** when the weekly question is which channel produced **Stripe (or similar) revenue**, not only traffic. Connect a processor, then pass visitor/session IDs into checkout metadata. That path is documented on [Fathom vs DataFast](/compare/fathom-vs-datafast/) and [Stripe revenue attribution](/learn/stripe-revenue-attribution/).

Be honest about cookies: DataFast’s [homepage FAQ](https://datafa.st/#pricing) and [GDPR / cookieless docs](https://datafa.st/docs/gdpr-cookieless-tracking) (both opened **24 November 2026**) say the **default** script uses cookies for returning visitors and the strongest revenue matching. The **cookieless** script (`script.cookieless.js`) does not use cookies for visitor IDs; identifiers rotate about every **24 hours** UTC, which weakens multi-day journeys and revenue attribution and drops User/Journey-style returning-visitor reports. If “website analytics without cookies” is a hard requirement **and** you sell online, Fathom plus a valued `trackEvent` is the stricter cookieless option; DataFast cookieless is the compromise.

### Many sites on one invoice

**Pick Fathom.** Fifty sites are included on Standard and Business at the 100k stop. Plausible Starter is **one site**; Growth is **up to three**. Umami Hobby is **one website**. DataFast Starter is **one website**.

### Open source or self-hosted

**Pick [Umami](/tools/umami/)** for MIT-licensed Docker-style ops, or **Umami Cloud Hobby** if **$0 / 100k events** is enough. **Pick [Plausible CE](https://plausible.io/docs/self-hosting)** only after you accept twice-yearly releases and Cloud-only features (funnels, user journeys, ecommerce revenue goals, SSO, Sites API). **Pick [Matomo On-Premise](/tools/matomo/)** when you need GA-like reports and will run PHP/MySQL. Primer: [self-hosted web analytics](/learn/self-hosted-web-analytics/).

[Fathom Lite](https://usefathom.com/pricing/lite) is a **free self-hosted** download with fewer metrics and **no vendor support**. It is not hosted Fathom in a container. DataFast has **no** self-hosted edition.

### Already paying for Ahrefs SEO

**Pick [Ahrefs Web Analytics](/tools/ahrefs/)** for verified projects: the [product page](https://ahrefs.com/web-analytics) (24 November 2026) calls it cookie-free and **free up to 1 million events** per project per month. Paid add-on dollar amounts were **not** on that page today, so they are omitted here.

### Leaving GA4 for GDPR, not for features

Stay on the [GA4 alternatives for GDPR](/learn/ga4-alternatives-gdpr/) shortlist (Plausible, Fathom, Umami, Matomo). This page is the pricing and cookie matrix around that shortlist. Keep GA4 if Google Ads or BigQuery is weekly work.

sections.title: Cookieless hosted vs self-hosted privacy
sections.content:
**Cookieless hosted SaaS** (Fathom, Plausible Cloud, Ahrefs Web Analytics, DataFast cookieless mode) minimizes ops: paste a script, update the privacy policy, pay a traffic tier. Best when nobody wants to run a database.

**Self-hosted privacy** (Umami, Matomo On-Premise, Plausible CE, Fathom Lite) keeps the analytics database on infrastructure you control. Best when residency, air-gapped networks, or high-volume Cloud invoices beat setup time. You become the operator for patches, backups, and “where does this live?”

These goals are not exclusive. Matomo Cloud and Umami Cloud sit in the middle: same brand, vendor-run stack. Matomo Cloud data is stored in **Frankfurt, Germany** per [Matomo pricing FAQ](https://matomo.org/pricing/) (24 November 2026). Plausible Cloud visitor data stays on **EU-owned** infrastructure in Germany per [Plausible’s privacy page](https://plausible.io/privacy-focused-web-analytics). Fathom’s [data journey](https://usefathom.com/data) describes EU isolation for EU visitors, then anonymized processing; hosted Fathom is **not** something you install locally ([features FAQ](https://usefathom.com/features): “Can I host the data locally? No.”).

Umami Cloud servers are in the **US and EU** per [Umami pricing FAQ](https://umami.is/pricing). That is a different residency story than Plausible Cloud.

Directory feature flags (`cookieless`, `self_hosted`) match this split except where noted: Matomo is `cookieless: false` in [our snapshot](/tools/matomo/) because cookies are the default; the vendor documents an optional cookieless mode with known accuracy loss. DataFast is `cookieless: true` in [our snapshot](/tools/datafast/) because a cookieless script exists — the **default** install still uses cookies. Follow the vendor docs above, not the convenient flag.

sections.title: Current pricing notes (do not trust a year-old roundup)
sections.content:
Roundups rot because vendors ship new plan **shapes**, not only new dollar amounts. Two of those shape changes matter on this page.

### Fathom: Standard vs Business, still billed by pageviews

[Fathom pricing](https://usefathom.com/pricing) (slider JSON on the page, **24 November 2026**) still has pageview stops. **Standard** (“personal” in that JSON) at those stops: **$15 / 100k**, **$25 / 200k**, **$45 / 500k**, **$60 / 1M**, **$100 / 2M**, **$140 / 5M**, **$200 / 10M**, then **$290 / 15M**, **$380 / 20M**, **$470 / 25M**. **Business** at the same stops: **$39**, **$49**, **$89**, **$119**, **$199**, **$239**, **$299**, **$439**, **$569**, **$699**. Included sites scale from **50** (through 500k) to **75 / 100 / 150 / 200 / 250 / 300 / 350** at the higher stops. Yearly is **10×** monthly (two months free). Over 25M is Custom.

The FAQ line “Standard and Business both cover 100,000 to 25 million pageviews” means both **families** exist across that range — it does **not** mean $15 includes 25M. You still pick a pageview stop. Our [Fathom directory](/tools/fathom/) still stores only the old single-ladder **$15–$200** Standard amounts (checked 19 Nov 2026) and has **no Business column**. Treat that JSON as **stale on plan shape**; the dollars for Standard still match today’s slider.

### Plausible: three Cloud plans, new 5M/10M Starter prices

[Plausible’s homepage widget](https://plausible.io/) (24 November 2026) prices **Starter / Growth / Business** on the same pageview steps. Starter: **$9 / 10k**, **$19 / 100k**, **$29 / 200k**, **$49 / 500k**, **$69 / 1M**, **$89 / 2M**, **$129 / 5M**, **$169 / 10M**. Our [Plausible directory](/tools/plausible/) still stores an August 2026 **single** ladder and lists **$109 / 5M** and **$149 / 10M**. Follow the widget; that snapshot is stale on both shape and the top two Starter rungs.

[Subscription-plan docs](https://plausible.io/docs/subscription-plans) (page last updated 29 October 2026; opened today): **30-day trial, no card**, Business features during the trial. Custom events count toward usage; a pageview **goal** does not.

### DataFast, Umami, Matomo, Ahrefs

**DataFast:** confirm [the homepage widget](https://datafa.st/#pricing) before you buy. FAQ copy we could read today: Starter vs Growth allowances above; event bands **10k, 100k, 200k, 1M+**; **14-day free trial, no card**. Dollar amounts in our directory (Starter **$9** at 10k events, then **$19 / 100k**, **$29 / 200k**, **$49 / 500k**, **$69 / 1M**, **$89 / 2M**, **$129 / 5M**, **$169 / 10M**; Growth **$19** at 10k) were last stored **11 November 2026**. We could not re-read those dollars from static HTML today.

**Umami Cloud:** [pricing](https://umami.is/pricing) — Hobby **$0**, **100k** events, **1** website, **6 months** retention, community support. Pro: **1 million** events included then **$0.00003** per extra event, up to **20** websites, **2 years** retention. Business: **10 million** events then **$0.00002** extra, unlimited websites, **5 years** retention, **5,000** session replays included then **$0.005** each, heatmaps. Self-hosted is included as the open-source app; [Cloud vs self-hosted](https://docs.umami.is/docs/cloud) (opened today) says **email reports are Cloud only**. The public pricing page did not expose a Pro **list price** in the HTML we parsed today, so that dollar is omitted. Our [Umami directory](/tools/umami/) still says Pro includes **10** sites and `heatmaps: false` — vendor pages today say Pro is **20** websites and heatmaps sit on **Cloud Business** (and self-hosted v3.2+ per Umami’s Cloud docs). Follow the vendor.

**Matomo Cloud:** use **USD $26** at 50k hits from [pricingforai](https://matomo.org/pricingforai/) (24 November 2026): then **$42 / 100k**, **$85 / 300k**, **$139 / 600k**, **$204 / 1M**, **$399 / 2M**, **$975 / 5M**, 10M+ contact. The marketing widget still showed a **29 / month excl. tax** headline without a currency in the HTML. On-Premise Community software is **free**; plugin bundles start at **€230 / €1,209 / €2,834** per month for Team / Business / Enterprise ([pricing](https://matomo.org/pricing/)).

**Ahrefs:** free tier only, as quoted above. Higher “upgrade” prices were not on the public product page we opened.

sections.title: Next steps
sections.content:
1. Name the job: **traffic without cookies**, **revenue by channel**, **self-host**, or **GA-like depth**.
2. Read the matching pair: [Plausible vs Fathom](/compare/plausible-vs-fathom/) or [Fathom vs DataFast](/compare/fathom-vs-datafast/). Deeper suite vs simple hosted: [Plausible vs Matomo](/compare/matomo-vs-plausible/). Open-source twins: [Plausible vs Umami](/compare/plausible-vs-umami/).
3. Confirm today’s price on the vendor page linked in the table — then sanity-check volume in the [pricing calculator](/calculators/pricing/).
4. If the site is a **blog** and the job is top posts plus newsletter and affiliate clicks, use [best analytics for a blog](/learn/best-analytics-for-a-blog/) instead of stretching this shortlist.

This page is not legal advice. “Privacy-first” and “privacy-friendly” describe product design, not a certificate that you can skip counsel.
